content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Kubient's indemnity satisfies the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

| Preferred element | Status |
|---|---|
| Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer + affiliated persons | ✅ p0047 (officers, directors, managers, members, agents, employees) |
| Third-party IP infringement | ✅ via Services/Auction Platform limbs + warranty limb feeding off p0039–p0040 IP-ownership warranties |
| Vendor breach of law | ✅ warranty limb + p0041 compliance warranty |
| Vendor-caused data breach / gross negligence / wilful misconduct | ✅ acts-or-omissions limb (p0051) |
| Notice, control, cooperation | ✅ p0053–p0055, with late notice not relieving the indemnitor (pro-AP) |
| Customer indemnity stays narrow | ✅ p0052 keyed to AP Content/Properties and AP's own conduct; no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's Services |

The indemnity is also effectively uncapped in AP's favour, since p0027 carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion and no super-cap is imposed — so the fallback's 3× annual fees ceiling is unnecessary.

Two minor sub-elements sit short of ideal wording and were recorded in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements:
- the Creative limb (p0050) carries a "to the best of its knowledge" knowledge qualifier;
- AP's indemnity reaches slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law, extending to "unauthorized or inappropriate use" and breach of any representation or warranty.

Worth noting for the broader review, though outside this rule's scope: p0028 imposes a one-year limitation period on any action, which would practically compress the window for enforcing these indemnities — a matter for the dispute-resolution/limitations rule rather than a second flag on the same commercial term here.
